machine.topology: inner rotor, one V-shaped pocket per pole holding two flat NdFeB magnets, notched rotor surface; 48 round-bottomed slots, single-layer distributed winding (q = 2)
machine.symmetry: One pole of eight (45 degrees) with antiperiodic radial ends and a sliding band in the gap that turns the rotor without remeshing; flux linkages times 8, the band's torque is the machine's. Locked-rotor positions beyond a pole pitch are taken a pitch back with negated currents.

emf_test_oil_temperature_C.quote: The lubricating oil temperature during this motor test was a nominal 25°C

magnet_temperature_C.reason: The magnets are taken at the back-EMF test's nominal 25 C oil temperature (the unenergized rotor spun in oil near room temperature). The locked-rotor tests' temperature is not stated; the report notes rotor heating was a concern, so a hotter rotor would lower the measured torque.

steel_bh.reason: The lamination grade is not stated (0.33 mm sheets, Table 2.7). FEMM's library M-19 (14 mil, 0.36 mm), a common high-grade non-oriented silicon steel of nearly the stated thickness, is taken; control steel-m36 uses the library's M-36 14 mil.
steel_bh.note: FEMM 5 matlib.dat, Soft Magnetic Materials/Silicon Iron, M-19 14 mil; the (0, 0) point dropped.

stacking_factor.reason: Not stated. The stated stator core mass (19.05 kg) over the drawn lamination area (29,650 mm2 with the bolt ears) and the 84 mm stack gives 7.65 g/cm3 at a fill of 1.00, which a 0.33 mm silicon steel (7.60-7.70 g/cm3) and the stack's rounding (8.35-8.45 cm) put between 0.98 and 1.00; 0.99 is the middle. Control stacking-factor-0p96 takes a common data-sheet value.

shaft_material.reason: The laminations sit on a large-diameter rotor shaft (TM-2010/253: earlier designs have a rotor shaft with a much larger OD; the 10.2 kg rotor mass includes it); its material is not stated and is taken as a low-carbon steel (FEMM's library 1010 Steel (hot rolled), as ShaftSteel). Control shaft-air makes it non-magnetic.

test_current_scale.reason: Table 3.2's current is taken as the amplitude of the test's current vector (Ia = I, Ib = Ic = -I/2). Evidence: 337 N m at 250 A matches the dynamometer map's 269.7 N m at 129.8 A rms (184 A peak) and the thermal report's 167.3 N m at 81.6 A rms (115 A peak) when the currents are peaks; an rms reading contradicts both. Control test-current-line-to-line takes 2/sqrt(3) times the current: dc fed from one terminal to another.

reference_angle_deg.figure: MAIN Table 3.2 (p. 20) and Fig. 3.9 (p. 19): the motor-shaft angle at which the current vector lies on the rotor's d-axis
reference_angle_deg.scale_reference: the curves' zero crossings: at 150-250 A the torque falls through zero between 90 and 92 degrees (90.64, 90.77, 91.00 by interpolation) and, extrapolated from 132-134 degrees, rises through zero again at 134.7-136.0 degrees (minus 45: 89.7-91.0); their mean, 90.6
reference_angle_deg.note: The narrow negative lobe right after this angle is the reluctance torque of Lq > Ld (the report: 'Lq is greater than Ld'), so here the current lies on the positive d-axis and the electrical angle from the d-axis to the current grows as 4 (angle - 90.6) degrees. The low-current curves cross less cleanly (cogging).

rotor_contours.figure: ORNL/TM-2005/33 Fig. 21 (p. 25) as vector art: the blue rotor pocket strokes, in the frame of the pole axis
rotor_contours.scale_reference: x and y scaled separately (the rotor circle is drawn as an ellipse, x/y = 1.01139) so that it has the stated 6.314 in diameter; the stated 4.356, 6.375 and 10.600 in diameters then read 4.3582, 6.3824 and 10.6048 in
rotor_contours.note: One V pocket and its two magnets in the pole frame (pole axis along +x), turned to 22.5 degrees by entity_pattern. The pocket is pole 7's closed stroke simplified within 0.05 mm, each vertex the mean of the nearest vertex of all eight drawn pockets and their mirror images (the pockets are symmetric about 22.5 + 45 k degrees within 0.02 degrees, mirror mismatch 0.05 mm), and the upper half mirrored. The magnets are the stated 18.9 x 6.5 mm sections on the pocket's straight inner edge, centred between the nose and step faces that hold them (0.2 mm play each end). Uncertainty: the drawing's 0.06 pt coordinate step (0.08 mm).

notch_angle_deg.scale_reference: as rotor_contours; the mean of the 16 dips' angles from their pole axes (11.441-11.509)

gaps.note: From the zero crossings of Table 3.2's high-current curves (both the d-axis and the reversed d-axis crossing), 90.6 +- 0.4 degrees; the 90-electrical-degree ambiguity the skill guards against does not arise, since the curve's own asymmetry (a narrow negative lobe of reluctance torque) fixes which crossing is the d-axis.

findings: No acceptance target from the paper passes; only the construction's phase-linkage check does (balanced phases in the A-B-C order). Every measured quantity is exceeded by a nearly uniform factor: the line-to-line back-EMF constant is 1.598 V/Hz against 1.338 (+19.4%; fundamental 1.590), and the locked-rotor peak torque is 85.1, 134.3, 180.2, 224.8, 264.0, 335.1 and 398.6 N m against Table 3.2's 74.0, 117.7, 158.0, 199.0, 229.0, 286.6 and 339.0 at 50-250 A (+14.9, +14.1, +14.1, +13.0, +15.3, +16.9, +17.6%). The Table 3.4 rms points are 16-27% high (the 502 rpm point most) and the peaks 10-19% high.

The shapes are reproduced. Each model curve correlates with its Table 3.2 column at 0.998-0.999 and fits it as 1.13-1.18 times the measurement with a residual of 1.9-3.0% of the peak; the measured curves' irregular bumps (from slot ripple between the 2 degree samples) appear at the same shaft angles in the model, which confirms the reference angle read from the zero crossings (90.6 degrees) and the winding axis. The model's line-to-line peak-to-rms ratio is 1.554 against the table's 1.57 (850/539.8). Splitting each curve into A sin(gamma) + B sin(2 gamma): the magnet term is 1.15-1.22 times the measured one and the reluctance term 1.07-1.14 times.

Representation and numerics are not the cause. A full cross-section (242k elements, diagnostic outside the case) gives the sector's flux linkage within 0.002% and its torque within 0.02-0.05% at 0, 96 and 122 degrees and 100-250 A. The mesh at 0.7 times (51,949 elements) changes no acceptance value by more than 0.1%. Torque from the flux linkages, 3/2 p (psi_d iq - psi_q id), differs from the band's by up to 41 N m on the negative lobe at 250 A (slot-ripple torque the dq formula leaves out); the band's value is the one that matches the test there (-42.8 against -46.2 N m at 96 degrees).

Controls move every acceptance value by less than 5%: the drawing's 0.775 mm gap lowers the torques 0.2-1.8% and the EMF 0.4%; M-36 steel the torques 0.9-1.5%; a 0.96 fill the torques 0.2-2.8% (most at high current) and raises the EMF 0.5%; an air shaft lowers the torques 0.7-2.2% and leaves the EMF; magnets at 60 C lower the EMF 4.1% and the torques 1.4-2.8%, still leaving every target 11-15% high. Feeding the test current line to line (2/sqrt 3) raises the torques a further 12-18%, so the stated current is the vector's amplitude, as the load tests indicated.

The stator side agrees with the machine: the model's low-current inductances (diagnostic from the run's flux linkages at 50 A) are Lq 5.06-5.10 mH and Ld 2.04-2.07 mH against the report's static 5 and 1.92 mH, and 72 series turns of 13 AWG 19 strands give 0.060 ohm plus leads against 0.069 and 6.7 kg of copper against 6.8. The magnet side does not: the model's phase magnet flux linkage is 0.2066 Wb against 0.173 implied by the measured back-EMF, which the thermal report's no-load test confirms independently (80-85 V line to line at 60 Hz with only 1.5-3.5 A, so the EMF is 78-82 V there).

Diagnostic outside the case: with the remanence lowered from 1.255 to 1.051 T at 20 C (so the magnet term matches), the back-EMF is 1.294 V/Hz (-3.3%), the Table 3.4 points -6% to +3%, and the peaks +0.9, +2.4, +4.8, +3.1, +5.5, +8.5 and +9.6% from 50 to 250 A: the low-current torque follows, but the reluctance term stays 10-16% high. The whole set instead behaves as the model times 0.86 at every current (an effective length near 72 mm), which the stated 84 mm stack, the 3.3 in stack of Table 4.1 and the 19.05 kg core mass (7.65 g/cm3 at full fill) rule out as a length.

Cause open. The leading candidates are installed magnets weaker than the hysteresisgraph sample of Fig. 2.72 (or not fully magnetized), together with 3D effects a 2D model omits (magnet ends 0.45 mm short of the stack at each end, end plates, end leakage), and a lamination steel or stress state that saturates sooner than M-19 at high current. The failures are kept as reviewed findings; nothing frozen was changed.
Cogging over the no-load sweep is 4.55 N m peak to peak (a model value; the report gives none).

Sources disagree on the air gap: Table 2.7 gives 0.73025 mm, the drawing's 6.314 in rotor in its 6.375 in bore 0.7747 mm, and the drawing's own strokes 0.86 mm (its bore reads 6.3824 in at the rotor's scale). The model used Table 2.7; the control shows the choice moves results by at most 2%.
retrospective: Outcome first (held-out, skill 713906e, no skill or lesson edits): failed, 1 of 9 acceptance checks (the phase linkage); every paper target 13-19% high with the shapes reproduced. Times: intake 7 min (stopped for TM-2010/253), extraction to freeze 31 min, solve 40 min (run1 with seven controls, plus a full cross-section and one remanence diagnostic in parallel), investigation and record about 35 min.

Longest: the rotor geometry. The lamination drawing is vector art, pasted with x/y scales 1.1% apart; reading it needed a stroke reader, an ellipse fit for the two scales, averaging over eight poles and their mirror images, and seating the stated magnets between the pocket's nose and step faces. Generic result: femm_brain/vector_figure.py.

The skill lacked: (1) an intake check that every source the index entry relies on is cached (TM-2010/253 held the stack length, turns and circuits; the stop was correct and cheap); (2) a step for figures that are vector art inside a PDF (pdfimages -list shows no raster on the page; convert with pdftocairo -svg and read the strokes; fit a drawn circle to detect unequal scales); (3) a pre-freeze plausibility estimate of each measured target from the frozen inputs (a one-line magnetic-circuit estimate gives B1 about 0.87 T against the 0.74 T the measured EMF implies, a 16% gap visible before solving); (4) guidance for locked-rotor tests: reproduce the procedure (fixed current vector, rotor turned) rather than a current-angle sweep, and keep a sliding band within one sector by taking positions a pole pitch back with every current negated.

Proposed lessons (generic): measured EMF and torque that both exceed a 2D model by one factor while inductances match point at the magnets or 3D magnet effects, not at turns or length (turns scale reluctance torque as N squared, length scales inductance too); separate the magnet and reluctance terms by fitting A sin(gamma) + B sin(2 gamma) to locked-rotor curves; a stated core mass with the drawn lamination area bounds the stacking factor; a test-current convention can be settled from independent load tests (torque against rms current at speed); a reference angle taken from a curve's own zero crossings is confirmed when the curve's fine slot-ripple structure lines up after solving, and then needs no 90-degree control; the flux-linkage torque formula misses large slot-ripple torque near the d-axis at high current.

Lessons that held: compare shapes as well as values (ibrahim-2016-synrm: a uniform factor with the shape reproduced points at a scale); estimate the element count before freezing (estimate 19-25k, actual 28,943); check a sector model against the full cross-section (agreement 0.002%); FEMM's air-gap-element torque of a sector is the machine's.

Allowances: the frozen 5% (back-EMF) and 10% (torque) allowances were built from input uncertainties; the observed systematic is 13-19%. For measured targets on production machines the skill could ask for the magnet data's provenance (a sample's hysteresis curve against the installed magnets) as an explicit uncertainty.

Generic changes made: femm_brain/vector_figure.py (strokes of PDF pages, unequal-scale ellipse fit, chaining, simplification); waveform_statistic rms and peak of the band-limited waveform and its time derivative (EMF rms and peak with harmonics); the step_statistic assessor (maximum, minimum or mean over a sweep that is not an even rotor period). The stator was drawn as data-only polylines and arcs over quoted dimensions because trapezoidal_slot_stator has neither a round slot bottom nor a sector option; adding both (and re-verifying its evidence) would make it a component.
